card.summary: 2 active HTTP and HTTPS tunnels, no time limit

free_tier.stated: 2 active HTTP and HTTPS tunnels, no time limit

retention.stated: not applicable: no session cap on the free tier

record.chaining: a free persistent tunnel for two services with no published byte quota, so it composes with an origin and cannot be sized in advance.
record.reliability_note: Free tunnels are HTTP and HTTPS only, time limited, and serve an interstitial warning page to visitors

evidence.proved: 2 active HTTP/HTTPS tunnels on the free tier and the definition of an active tunnel
Starter lists HTTP and HTTPS tunnels only; PRO adds 'HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, TLS, UDP tunneling' and 'TCP, UDP port forwarding'

record.notes: No byte quota is published, and none is needed to decide: the free tier cannot carry UDP. The vendor's own pages disagree on whether free bandwidth is unlimited, which is why the number is not recorded as such: a January 2026 blog post says '2 HTTP tunnels with unlimited bandwidth', while the September 2026 free-port-forwarding page says raw TCP and UDP forwarding and unlimited bandwidth are Pro. Unmeasured. Records the vendor's internal contradiction instead of silently picking a side.

extras.transit_note: the tunnel relays the origin's bytes; no byte quota is published

record.limits_note: counts of things, not rates, so no vocabulary kind names them: 2 concurrently active tunnels; an active tunnel is any tunnel currently running
record.binding_note: The free plan publishes no bandwidth figure at all: the pricing page lists 'Unlimited bandwidth' under the USD 8 Pro row only, and the free row's stated negatives are 'Time limits' and 'Interstitial warning page'. UDP and TCP forwarding are Pro features, so the ingress test fails before a byte is counted and the volume question never arises.
